title: Rupee rises 43 paise to close at 93.51 (provisional) against US dollar - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The rupee appreciated by 43 paise to close at 93.51 against the US dollar on Tuesday, on the back of softer crude oil prices, upbeat domestic markets, and foreign fund inflows even as a strong dollar and elevated US bond yields limited the upside.

Forex traders said fresh foreign fund inflows and softer crude oil prices are supporting the rupee, while a stronger dollar and rising US yields remain key risks.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.72 against the dollar. During intra-day trade, it hit a high of 93.40 and a low of 93.73. The local unit settled at 93.51 (provisional), higher by 43 paise from its previous close.

On Monday, the rupee appreciated by 25 paise to close at 93.94 against the US dollar.

"We expect the rupee to trade with a positive bias on a decline in crude oil prices and positive domestic markets. Sustained foreign inflows may also support the rupee.

"However, a strong greenback and rising US Treasury yields may cap sharp upside. Traders may take cues from retail sales and industrial production data from the US. USDINR spot price is expected to trade in a range of 93.20 to 93.75," Anuj Choudhary, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan.

Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.54, lower by 0.01 per cent.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.38 per cent lower at $92.79 per barrel in futures trade.

In the domestic equity market, the Sensex climbed 427.40 points to settle at 82,532.19, while the Nifty was up 96.30 points at 25,387.40.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹4,864.68 crore on Monday, according to exchange data.
